name: MCR in CMNS
full_name: Multifunctional magnetic catheter robot (MCR) in a closed-loop magnetic navigation system (CMNS)
group: G. Jang, Department of Mechanical Engineering, Hanyang University
versions: CMNS hardware: 8 electromagnets at the vertices of a hexahedron with a back yoke (nam2018_magnetic); MCR with steering, tunnelling and stent-delivery motions (lee2021_steering, online 2020-01-15, IEEE TIE 68(1) 2021)
target_anatomy: occlusive vascular disease (angioplasty: steering, clot tunnelling, stent delivery) (lee2021_steering Sec. I)
devices_driven: own MCR: tube with a diametrically magnetized front magnet and drill tip, magnetic joint, two tension springs (26 N/m total), self-expandable stent; max OD 3.5 mm (about 10 Fr), min ID 0.4 mm passes a 0.014-in guidewire (lee2021_steering Sec. IV-A)
n_dof_detail: field direction, magnitude and rotation from 8 electromagnets: steering (static field), tunnelling (rotating field), stent release (field magnitude) (lee2021_steering Sec. II-C)
rotation_detail: rotating field (20 mT, 12 Hz) spins the front magnet and drill tip for tunnelling (lee2021_steering Sec. IV-B)
footprint_mm: cylindrical workspace up to 500 diameter (lee2021_steering Sec. II-B)
imaging_compat: biplane cameras (CMOS, 30 fps) only (lee2021_steering Sec. II-B, IV-B)
validation_detail: in vitro only: obstacle table with 4 steering points; stent-release threshold in a straight glass tube (10 trials); stent deployment accuracy in a branched 8 mm glass tube, 10 trials each for MCR and a conventional catheter; Y-shaped water-filled glass tube with a 5% agar clot: steer, tunnel, deploy stent, return (lee2021_steering Sec. IV)
key_numbers: steering at 20 mT; tunnelling at 20 mT, 12 Hz; stent release at 78.5 mT on average (theory 59 mT), 100% above 80 mT; stent position error 2.30 +/- 0.34 mm vs 8.79 +/- 0.69 mm for a conventional delivery catheter (lee2021_steering Sec. IV-B)
sim_model: none found (dynamic model of the magnetic joint for design, lee2021_steering Sec. III)
